action: Engine generates dataset samples every 5 minutes via a cron job, using the local fine-tuned model which has no rate limits and costs nothing.

flags.reason: The local fine-tuned model is idle between 5-minute cron ticks despite having no rate limits and zero cost; an owned asset that can work is not being kept working continuously.
A rigid 5-minute cron cadence is artificial batching with no stated real constraint; continuous generation should replace the timer unless a hard limit is proven.
No receipt, artifact hash, or failure signal is specified for each generated dataset batch; silent cron failures would violate visible-output requirements.

summary: Cron-batched generation underutilizes a free local model, imposes an artificial cadence, and lacks a visible receipt.

action: The propose/verify engine uses the local fine-tuned model as the generator, with the free cloud lanes (OpenRouter free tier) configured as fallback only when the local model fails.

flags.reason: Free cloud lanes are configured as fallback-only, so they sit idle whenever the local model succeeds; owned capacity that can work isn't working.
Independent cloud sources are fallback-only instead of running in parallel, directly violating the parallel-sources requirement.
No machine-checkable probe verdict is specified for the local-model-as-generator + cloud-fallback change.
Fallback activation can silently degrade results without a receipt; the action doesn't guarantee visible output on fallback.
No independent reviewer is mentioned for the propose/verify engine — if the same model proposes and verifies, it's self-review.

summary: Local generator with cloud fallback violates parallel-utilization, probe, and independent-review rules.

action: Fine-tuned model trained and adopted, deployed as a local lane, but no production traffic routed to it yet; routing build scheduled for later.

flags.reason: Fine-tuned model is deployed as a local lane but receives no production traffic — an owned asset that can work is idle, violating capacity utilization.
Routing is 'scheduled for later' with no real constraint stated; this is artificial batching/delay, violating continuous-over-batched.
No derived deadline is shown for routing; any schedule must be effort/machine-hours divided by measured lane rate, and none is provided.
Model adoption and lane deployment shipped without a machine-checkable probe verdict — probe-gating is mandatory for model/lane changes.
Training, adoption, and deployment are ledger-worthy actions but no independent review is mentioned — self-review is prohibited.

summary: Adopting and deploying the lane without traffic, probe evidence, derived timing, or independent review violates multiple core rules.

action: Launch timeline estimated as: capability layer 2-4 days, instructions 08-25, pilot 08-31, cohort 09-14, based on a sequential plan.

flags.reason: Deadlines (08-25, 08-31, 09-14) are not derived from effort/machine-hours divided by any measured lane rate; no rate source is cited.
Timeline is expressed in human days (2-4 days) and dates, not machine-hours, violating machine-time scheduling/reporting.
The plan is explicitly sequential; independent capability, instruction, pilot, and cohort workstreams should run in parallel where dependencies allow, not as fallback-only chains.
Fixed milestone dates appear to impose artificial cadence without demonstrating a real constraint requiring batching/serialization.
Sequential plan leaves owned assets idle while later stages wait, instead of keeping every capable asset working continuously.
Sequential gating creates a single-chain bottleneck where later stages wait on prior stage completion, contrary to self-executing in-bounds work.
The action produces no receipt/verifiable artifact; timeline estimates ship without an observable output or machine-checkable evidence.

summary: Sequential day-based timeline violates rate-derived deadlines, machine-hours reporting, parallel execution, continuous utilization, and receipt requirements.

action: A background bridge service was deployed; it crash-looped 1273 times over an hour before being noticed during a user request.

flags.reason: Crash-looped 1273 times over an hour with no receipt or alert; degradation was silent until a user request surfaced it.
Service shipped without a machine-checkable probe verdict; a probe would have caught the crash loop immediately.
Owned asset was not in a working state for an hour while capable infrastructure idled in a failing loop.

summary: Unprobed deploy crash-looped silently for an hour — violates visibility, probe-gating, and utilization.

action: Attestation heartbeat attests ledger rows after they are committed; nothing reviews changes before they ship.

flags.reason: Ledger-worthy changes ship with no independent review before commit; the attestation heartbeat is post-hoc and does not satisfy independent challenge.
No pre-ship review receipt exists; only post-commit attestation, so unreviewed changes can ship silently before any visible output flags them.

summary: Changes ship unreviewed; post-commit attestation violates independent challenge and leaves pre-ship review invisible.
